LESSONS.title: Make a table
LESSONS.goal: Make a table and fill it with CREATE TABLE and INSERT
summary: connect(":memory:") is a temporary practice DB
CREATE TABLE makes a table
INSERT INTO … VALUES adds one row

cards.say: A database is a storeroom that keeps data in tables. connect(":memory:") is a temporary practice DB, so it vanishes when the run ends. CREATE TABLE makes a table and INSERT fills it. commit() locks in what you added.
cards.code:
import sqlite3
conn = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
cur = conn.cursor()
make = ("CREATE TABLE books "
        "(title TEXT, genre TEXT, "
        "year INTEGER)")
cur.execute(make)
add = ("INSERT INTO books VALUES "
    "('Moon Garden', 'novel', 2021)")
cur.execute(add)
conn.commit()
sel = ("SELECT title, year "
       "FROM books")
cur.execute(sel)
rows = cur.fetchall()
for r in rows:
    print(r[0], r[1])

cards.say: Text (TEXT) goes in single quotes; numbers (INTEGER) go without quotes. Chain groups in parentheses with commas after VALUES and you add several rows at once. SQL keywords are usually written in capitals.

LESSONS.title: Query with SELECT
LESSONS.goal: Use WHERE to take out only the rows that match a condition
summary: SELECT columns FROM table
Write the condition after WHERE
Text values in single quotes; equal is =

cards.say: SELECT picks which columns to take out, and WHERE filters which rows. Here we take only books from 2020 or later, in year order. (kids means children's books.)

LESSONS.title: Sort and summarize
LESSONS.goal: Use ORDER BY, COUNT, AVG and GROUP BY
summary: ORDER BY column DESC means largest first
COUNT(*) counts rows, AVG is the average
Group with GROUP BY, order with ORDER BY
SUM is the total; MAX and MIN are the largest and smallest

cards.say: ORDER BY column DESC sorts from largest to smallest. Add another column after a comma and it breaks ties. Here the newest books come first.

cards.say: GROUP BY groups books of the same genre so you can get COUNT (how many) and AVG (the average). When only one row comes back, fetchone() is handy. Grouped results get their order from ORDER BY too.

LESSONS.title: SQL from Python
LESSONS.goal: Add Python values to a DB safely with loops and ?
summary: Loop with for and call execute many times
? marks a value's spot; pass values as a tuple
Gluing text together is risky, so use ?

cards.say: Leave the spot for each value as ? in the SQL and pass the values separately as a tuple. Then for can add the books in a list one at a time.
cards.code:
import sqlite3
conn = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
cur = conn.cursor()
make = ("CREATE TABLE books "
        "(title TEXT, genre TEXT, "
        "year INTEGER)")
cur.execute(make)
ins = ("INSERT INTO books "
       "VALUES (?, ?, ?)")
new = [("Moon Garden", "novel", 2021),
       ("Tiny Forest", "kids", 2023)]
for b in new:
    cur.execute(ins, b)
sel = ("SELECT title FROM books "
       "ORDER BY title")
cur.execute(sel)
rows = cur.fetchall()
for r in rows:
    print(r[0])

cards.say: Even with one value, it's a tuple with a comma, like (value,). Gluing values into the SQL text is risky (SQL injection). Passing them with ? is safe. executemany adds a whole list at once.
